T: Hawker centre first. Then the family.
D: A New York professor flies to Singapore to meet her boyfriend's family and finds out they're incredibly rich.
P: Serve the snacks when Rachel gets her first taste of the hawker centre.
S: the night at the Singapore hawker centre
Chicken thighs marinated in turmeric, lemongrass and coconut, threaded onto skewers and grilled, with a peanut sauce.
the family folding dumplings together at the Young house
Pork and cabbage dumplings with ginger and spring onion, folded and boiled until they float, with black vinegar and chilli oil.
Peanuts roasted with garlic, chilli and salt until crunchy, served in small bowls beside the table.
M: Crab or big prawns cooked in a sweet, spicy sauce of tomato, chilli, garlic and ginger, finished with a beaten egg swirled through, with soft buns to mop up.
Egg noodles stir-fried with prawns, chicken and greens in oyster and soy sauce, piled high on a platter.
W: the Young family's grand home at Tyersall Park
Pandan chiffon cake of whipped egg whites, coconut milk and pandan, baked at 170C for 45 minutes and cooled upside down.
K: Strong coffee sweetened with condensed milk, poured over ice.

s.note: the night at the Singapore hawker centre
s.how: Marinate 600g chicken thigh strips in coconut milk, turmeric and finely chopped lemongrass for 2 hours. Thread onto skewers and grill until charred. Warm peanut butter with more coconut milk, lime juice and a little sugar for a thick dipping sauce.

s.note: the family folding dumplings together at the Young house
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with shredded wombok, grated ginger, sliced spring onion and salt. Fold into dumpling wrappers around the table together. Boil until they float, then a minute more. Serve with black vinegar for dipping.

m.how: Fry crushed garlic, grated ginger and chopped red chilli in oil. Add 150ml tomato sauce, a spoon of sugar and 200ml water and simmer. Add 1kg green prawns and cook 4 minutes. Swirl in 2 beaten eggs and serve with soft buns to mop up the sauce.

w.note: the Young family's grand home at Tyersall Park
w.how: Whisk 6 yolks with 60g sugar, 120ml coconut milk, 80ml oil and a teaspoon of pandan paste, then fold in 150g flour. Whisk 6 whites with 100g sugar to stiff peaks and fold in. Bake in an ungreased tube tin at 170C for 45 minutes and cool upside down.

d.how: Brew strong coffee and stir 2 tbsp condensed milk into each cup while hot until dissolved. Cool slightly, then pour over glasses packed with ice. Stir well and drink it the way the hawker stalls serve it, sweet and strong.
